slides.heading: Clinic and Home Visits
slides.subtitle: Two core delivery settings of community health nursing.

slides.heading: Clinic Visit
bullets: The client comes to the facility, mainly for consultation on physical complaints.
Registration/admission: greet & build rapport, prepare/retrieve family record, elicit chief complaint & history, perform & record PE.
Waiting time: priority numbers; first-come-first-served except emergencies.
Triaging: manage program-based cases; refer non-program cases to the physician; give first aid and refer emergencies.

slides.heading: Clinic Visit — Steps Continued
bullets: Clinical evaluation: validate history/PE, reach an evidence-based diagnosis, give rational DOH-based treatment, inform the client.
Laboratory: identify a designated referral lab when needed.
Referral: use the two-way referral system (BHS→RHU, RHU→RHU, RHU→hospital); accompany emergency referrals.
Prescription/dispensing: proper instructions on drug intake.
Health education: one-on-one counselling, reinforce messages, give next appointment.

slides.heading: Home Visit — Purpose
bullets: Give nursing care to the sick / postpartum mother & newborn, and teach a family member to continue care.
Assess living conditions and health practices to guide appropriate teaching.
Give health teaching on prevention and control of diseases.
Build a close relationship between health agencies and the public.
Use the inter-referral system and promote use of community services.

slides.heading: Steps in Conducting a Home Visit
bullets: Greet the patient and introduce yourself.
State the purpose of the visit.
Observe the patient and determine health needs.
Put the bag in a convenient place, then perform the bag technique.
Perform needed nursing care and give health teaching.
Record all important data, observations and care rendered.
Make an appointment for a return visit.

slides.heading: Key Takeaways
bullets: Clinic visit = client comes to the facility; home visit = nurse goes to the family.
Always use the two-way referral system and accompany emergency referrals.
Home visits also teach a responsible family member to continue care.
Every visit ends with documentation and a return appointment.
